title: A finite separable field extension tensored with a field extension is reduced
statement: Let $L$ be a field, let $K'/L$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension] ($K'$ a finite-dimensional $L$-vector space) which is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $E/L$ be any field extension. Then the ring $K'\otimes_LE$ (the tensor product of the $L$-algebras $K'$ and $E$, with multiplication $(a\otimes e)(a'\otimes e')=aa'\otimes ee'$ and unit $1\otimes1$) is reduced: it has no nonzero nilpotent elements.

proof.text: (Primitive element and presentation of $K'$.) Since $K'/L$ is finite and separable algebraic, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-primitive-element] gives $\alpha\in K'$ with $K'=L(\alpha)$. As $K'/L$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $\alpha$ is algebraic over $L$ and its minimal polynomial $P\in L[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is monic, irreducible, separable in the sense of [def-pc-separable-polynomial] (there are $U,V\in L[T]$ with $UP+VP'=1$), and generates the kernel of the $L$-algebra map $\varphi:L[T]\to K'$, $T\mapsto\alpha$ (all by [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]). By [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] (with $K=L$, $\Omega=K'$, $\theta=\alpha$) the powers $1,\alpha,\dots,\alpha^{d-1}$ form an $L$-basis of $L(\alpha)=K'$; they lie in the image of $\varphi$, which is an $L$-subspace, so $\varphi$ is surjective. Hence $\varphi$ induces an isomorphism of $L$-algebras $L[T]/(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}K'$, $T\bmod P\mapsto\alpha$.

proof.text: (Base change of the presentation.) Let $\bar P\in E[T]$ be the image of $P$ under the coefficient map $L[T]\to E[T]$ induced by $L\to E$. By step 1, $K'\otimes_LE\cong(L[T]/(P))\otimes_LE\cong E\otimes_L(L[T]/(P))$ as rings (the second map is the swap $x\otimes e\mapsto e\otimes x$). By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] (with $A=L$, $R=E$, $J$ a single index) the map $E\otimes_LL[T]\to E[T]$, $e\otimes p\mapsto e\bar p$, is an isomorphism of $E$-algebras; through it and the associativity isomorphism $E\otimes_L(L[T]/(P))\cong(E\otimes_LL[T])\otimes_{L[T]}(L[T]/(P))$, $e\otimes x\mapsto(e\otimes1)\otimes x$, we get $E\otimes_L(L[T]/(P))\cong E[T]\otimes_{L[T]}(L[T]/(P))$, with $E[T]$ an $L[T]$-algebra by the coefficient map. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with $A=L[T]$, $B=E[T]$, $I=(P)$, generated by the single element $P$) this is $E[T]/(\bar P)$. So there is a ring isomorphism $K'\otimes_LE\cong E[T]/(\bar P)$, sending $\alpha\otimes e$ to $eT\bmod\bar P$.

proof.text: ($\bar P$ is separable over $E$.) The coefficient map $c:L[T]\to E[T]$ is a ring homomorphism and commutes with the formal derivative, since both act coefficientwise ($c(\sum a_nT^n)'=\sum n\,c(a_n)T^{n-1}=c(P)'$ for each polynomial). Applying $c$ to $UP+VP'=1$ (step 1) gives $\bar U\bar P+\bar V\bar P'=1$ in $E[T]$, so $\bar P$ is separable over $E$ [def-pc-separable-polynomial].

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-separable-polynomial-quotient-reduced] (with $Q=\bar P$), the ring $E[T]/(\bar P)$ is reduced. A ring isomorphic to a reduced ring is reduced (an isomorphism maps nilpotents to nilpotents and only $0$ to $0$), so by step 2 $K'\otimes_LE$ is reduced.
